title: Autopsy fails to solve cause of man's death
article: An autopsy on a man who died shortly after he was arrested in a Rocky Mountain House restaurant on Sunday has been unable to pinpoint what caused his death.
Ted James Meiorin, 40, was wearing only his underwear and acting agitated in the restaurant's kitchen when RCMP were called to help around 5 p.m.
Shortly after two officers arrived, Meiorin apparently lunged at them. They restrained and arrested him, then called for an ambulance when they noticed something was wrong.
Meiorin died about 10 minutes after the police arrived.

RCMP spokesman Cpl. Wayne Oakes said the initial autopsy showed there were no obvious signs of trauma, so the medical examiner's office will now be doing forensic tests to try to establish why Meiorin died.
But RCMP are also looking to the community for more clues.

"We are appealing to the public for anyone who saw the incident, saw Meiorin prior to 5 p.m. or anybody who knew him on a regular or casual basis to come forward and provide information to investigators about what was going on in his life at this time," Oakes said.
